songs_to_prepare.title: Naughty
songs_to_prepare.why: Matilda's defining anthem — a child who decides the world's rules are wrong and acts on it

songs_to_prepare.title: My Favourite Things
songs_to_prepare.why: A child with a rich inner world and fierce intelligence in an unkind environment — warm child soprano

songs_to_prepare.title: Castle on a Cloud
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the lyric child quality and vulnerability beneath Matilda's formidable confidence

songs_to_prepare.title: Somewhere
songs_to_prepare.why: The yearning for a world where extraordinary people are not punished for it — Matilda in one song

matilda/matilda-matilda.style_guidance: Matilda requires a child who is genuinely extraordinary — a young soprano/belt with intelligence and physical commitment. She must read as preternaturally grown-up while being entirely a child. The belt range to E5 is needed.
avoid: Cute child performance — Matilda is never cute. She is fierce, compassionate, and righteous.

songs_to_prepare.title: The Hammer
songs_to_prepare.why: Trunchbull's own terrifying athletic number — character baritone/alto with physicality and menace

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am What I Am
songs_to_prepare.why: Absolute conviction of one's own righteousness — Trunchbull believes entirely in her methods

songs_to_prepare.title: Epiphany
songs_to_prepare.why: The gleeful expression of true malice — a character who enjoys causing harm

songs_to_prepare.title: I've Got a Little List
songs_to_prepare.why: Character voice cataloguing everything that must be destroyed — Trunchbull's entire worldview

matilda/matilda-trunchbull.style_guidance: Trunchbull is one of the great theatrical villains — baritone (traditional casting, often played by a man) or deep alto/character voice. The role demands physical extremity, total commitment, and genuine menace.
avoid: Comedic buffoon approach — Trunchbull is genuinely frightening. The comedy comes from scale, not from softness.

songs_to_prepare.title: This Is Me
songs_to_prepare.why: A person who has been invisible claiming their place — Honey's arc expressed in contemporary soprano terms

songs_to_prepare.title: I Dreamed a Dream
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano/mezzo who has survived cruelty and is still trying to hope — Honey's backstory exactly

songs_to_prepare.title: When I'm Stuck with a Day
songs_to_prepare.why: Miss Honey's own gentle number — warm soprano, protective love, and quiet courage

songs_to_prepare.title: So Big/So Small
songs_to_prepare.why: Maternal soprano with controlled emotion — a woman discovering her capacity to mother someone at last

matilda/matilda-miss-honey.style_guidance: Miss Honey is everything the show argues an adult should be — a soprano with warmth, gentleness, and quiet unflinching decency. She is timid in body and fearless in spirit. The voice should be clear and pure.
avoid: Operatic or heavy soprano approach — Honey is delicate light, not grandeur

songs_to_prepare.title: Master of the House
songs_to_prepare.why: The self-regarding idiot who genuinely believes he is brilliant — character baritone with physical comedy

songs_to_prepare.title: Razzle Dazzle
songs_to_prepare.why: The man who mistakes bluster for intelligence — baritone showmanship covering complete emptiness

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Broad character comedy energy for the show's resident buffoon who thinks he runs everything

matilda/matilda-mr-wormwood.style_guidance: Mr. Wormwood is the anti-Matilda — a character baritone who is loud, vain, stupid, and completely sincere about his own magnificence. Broad physical comedy essential. He should be genuinely funny, not just nasty.
avoid: Genuine malice — Wormwood is too stupid to be actually evil; he's a cartoon of ignorance

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm the Greatest Star
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who is absolutely convinced of her own specialness despite no actual evidence — mezzo belt comedy

songs_to_prepare.title: Everything's Coming Up Roses
songs_to_prepare.why: The mother who has invested entirely in the wrong things and will not examine why — belt and bravado

songs_to_prepare.title: Loud
songs_to_prepare.why: Mrs. Wormwood's own brash number — mezzo belt with sequins, self-delusion, and competitive dancing

matilda/matilda-mrs-wormwood.style_guidance: Mrs. Wormwood is sequins, spray tan, and competitive Latin dance — mezzo-soprano belt with enormous comic physicality. She resents Matilda personally for being clever instead of beautiful.
avoid: Subtlety — Mrs. Wormwood has never had a subtle thought in her life

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am What I Am
songs_to_prepare.why: The dancing partner who is entirely invested in his own glamour and Mrs. Wormwood's

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character tenor/baritone who exists as the comedy vehicle for Mrs. Wormwood's delusions

matilda/matilda-rudolpho.style_guidance: Rudolpho is the Latin dance partner — tenor/baritone character role with physical comedy, dance skill, and the specific flavour of someone thoroughly wrapped in Mrs. Wormwood's delusion.
avoid: Serious material — Rudolpho exists entirely within the comedy of the Wormwood world

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know
songs_to_prepare.why: The warm, observant mezzo who sees Matilda's genius and quietly champions it — warm mezzo character

songs_to_prepare.title: Children Will Listen
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — about caring adults and what they give children — Phelps's relationship with Matilda in song

matilda/matilda-mrs-phelps.style_guidance: Mrs. Phelps is the children's librarian who takes Matilda's remarkable mind seriously — warm mezzo with quiet intelligence. A supporting but important role; she is Matilda's first real ally.
avoid: Secondary, throwaway reading — Mrs. Phelps is the first adult who truly sees Matilda

songs_to_prepare.title: Do You Hear the People Sing
songs_to_prepare.why: The loyal comrade — child soprano who would follow Matilda anywhere and stands for justice

songs_to_prepare.title: Big Bright Beautiful World
songs_to_prepare.why: Cheerful child soprano with friendship energy — Lavender's devoted, loving nature

matilda/matilda-lavender.style_guidance: Lavender is Matilda's best friend and most devoted ally — child soprano with warmth, bravery, and a willingness to put newts in cups. Happy, bright, loyal.
avoid: Passive child reading — Lavender is an active co-conspirator with courage of her own

songs_to_prepare.title: Tomorrow
songs_to_prepare.why: The optimistic child who bounces back from punishment — Bruce never stops being fundamentally okay

songs_to_prepare.title: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown
songs_to_prepare.from: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown
songs_to_prepare.why: The good-natured kid who attracts misfortune without bitterness — Bruce completely

matilda/matilda-bruce.style_guidance: Bruce eats a whole chocolate cake in front of the school. He is an icon. Child treble with the ability to convey both terror and extraordinary food-related resolve. Warm and good-natured.
avoid: Dramatic heavy material — Bruce is fundamentally, lovably normal

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Loved You
songs_to_prepare.why: The father whose love was real — tenor/baritone showing warmth and tragedy beneath the showman persona

songs_to_prepare.title: Corner of the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The performer who found meaning and ultimately lost it — the showman with a real story

matilda/matilda-escapologist.style_guidance: The Escapologist appears in Matilda's stories as Miss Honey's father — tenor/baritone with theatrical flair and genuine warmth. He is a loving father and a victim. Brief but emotionally loaded role.
avoid: Cold or detached performance — the Escapologist must read as genuinely loving to make Honey's loss hurt

songs_to_prepare.title: In My Own Little Corner
songs_to_prepare.why: The brief, loving maternal presence — soprano who conveys warmth and swift loss

matilda/matilda-acrobat.style_guidance: The Acrobat is Miss Honey's mother — a fleeting soprano presence in the story that explains everything about who Honey became. Small role, enormous emotional impact.
avoid: Lengthy vocal showcasing — this is a brief appearance that carries specific grief

matilda/matilda-children-ensemble.role_name: Children's Ensemble — Students of Crunchem Hall

songs_to_prepare.title: Revolting Children
songs_to_prepare.why: The ensemble's defining number — children who have decided to rise up, full of anger and joy

songs_to_prepare.title: We're Not Gonna Take It
songs_to_prepare.why: If rock songs are accepted — Revolting Children energy in three words

songs_to_prepare.title: Tomorrow
songs_to_prepare.why: Child ensemble soprano/treble quality — shows the youthful brightness the children's scenes need

matilda/matilda-children-ensemble.style_guidance: The children of Crunchem Hall must be able to sing, act, and physically survive Trunchbull's school — youth ensemble with strong voices, physical commitment, and genuine ensemble storytelling instincts.
avoid: Adult performance style — the children must read as real children, not small adults pretending

matilda/matilda-adult-ensemble.role_name: Adult Ensemble — Doctors, Parents, Teachers, Townspeople

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Comic adult ensemble energy — the adults of Matilda's world are mostly oblivious and slightly satirised

songs_to_prepare.title: Anything Goes
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the period-adjacent charm the adult ensemble needs with comic intelligence

matilda/matilda-adult-ensemble.style_guidance: The adult ensemble supports the heightened world — Roald Dahl adults are generally comic, oblivious, or vile. Strong character work, period flavour, physical expressiveness.
avoid: Naturalistic acting school choices — the Dahl adult world is intentionally heightened satire

songs_to_prepare.title: Where Is Love
songs_to_prepare.why: Oliver's own longing song — clear, pure treble with genuine emotional simplicity and longing

songs_to_prepare.title: Castle on a Cloud
songs_to_prepare.why: The orphan's imagination sustaining them through grinding poverty — exact spiritual parallel

songs_to_prepare.title: Tomorrow
songs_to_prepare.why: The optimistic orphan who has not yet been broken — clean treble with natural resilience

oliver/oliver-twist.style_guidance: Oliver is the show's moral centre — an pure boy treble with natural emotional vulnerability and an instinct for goodness. He must be genuinely sympathetic, which requires real vocal purity and emotional honesty.
avoid: Street-hardened performance — Oliver is the boy who has not yet been corrupted, and that is the whole point

songs_to_prepare.title: Reviewing the Situation
songs_to_prepare.why: Fagin's great self-examination — character baritone with range to Eb5, humour, and genuine vulnerability

songs_to_prepare.title: You've Got to Pick a Pocket or Two
songs_to_prepare.why: Fagin's teaching number — shows the comedic warmth and showman quality the role requires

songs_to_prepare.title: Master of the House
songs_to_prepare.why: The canny operator who runs the criminal family — character baritone with warmth and calculation

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character energy of a man who manages chaos through personality — Fagin's fundamental skill

oliver/fagin.style_guidance: Fagin is the great character baritone role — warm, comic, genuinely caring in his criminal way, and ultimately a survivor. The voice needs enormous range (B2-Eb5), physical expressiveness, and the ability to be loveable and alarming simultaneously.
avoid: Playing Fagin as pure villain — he loves his boys; that's why Oliver trusts him and why the audience follows him

songs_to_prepare.title: As Long as He Needs Me
songs_to_prepare.why: Nancy's defining ballad — alto/mezzo belt showing an abused woman who loves completely, tragically

songs_to_prepare.title: It's a Fine Life
songs_to_prepare.why: Nancy performing happiness — mezzo belt with the specific tragedy of enforced cheerfulness

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Rain on My Parade
songs_to_prepare.why: The unstoppable woman who loves too much and pays for it — alto/mezzo belt anthem

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm Still Here
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who has survived everything life threw at her and won't stop fighting — Nancy's spirit

oliver/nancy.style_guidance: Nancy is one of musical theatre's great tragic heroines — alto/mezzo with a belt from E3 to B4, enormous warmth, and the ability to make love's self-destruction feel like strength rather than weakness.
avoid: Weak or passive reading — Nancy chooses her fate with both eyes open, and that choice must read as powerful

songs_to_prepare.title: Consider Yourself
songs_to_prepare.why: The Dodger's big recruitment number — treble/belt with showman charm and absolute street confidence

songs_to_prepare.title: I'd Do Anything
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the Dodger's natural leadership and playful manipulation — belt with character and ease

songs_to_prepare.title: Corner of the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The street kid who wants to be extraordinary and actually is — youth with ambition and swagger

oliver/artful-dodger.style_guidance: The Dodger is the show's energy source — treble/young belt with absolute physical swagger, leadership instinct, and the ability to charm every single person on stage and in the audience.
avoid: Playing criminal as dangerous — the Dodger is charming criminal, all performance and charisma, no genuine menace

songs_to_prepare.title: Stars
songs_to_prepare.why: Relentless pursuing bass-baritone who believes he is entitled — cold conviction, genuine threat

songs_to_prepare.title: Epiphany
songs_to_prepare.why: The moment when a man commits to violence without turning back — chilling, controlled, bass-baritone

songs_to_prepare.title: Old Man River
songs_to_prepare.why: Bass-baritone with physical weight and inevitability — Sikes as an immovable force

oliver/bill-sikes.style_guidance: Bill Sikes is the show's genuine monster — bass-baritone who must be truly frightening without theatrical excess. He is small, vicious, and specific. The audience must fear what he will do to Nancy.
avoid: Theatrical villainy — Sikes's menace comes from cold, contained realism, not performance

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: The pompous authority figure who exists to be outwitted — character baritone with maximum self-importance

songs_to_prepare.title: I've Got the Horse Right Here
songs_to_prepare.why: Blustering comic character who believes his own nonsense entirely

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character comedy baritone who cannot see what is obvious to the audience — Bumble in one song

oliver/mr-bumble.style_guidance: Mr Bumble is the beadle — pompous, venal, utterly self-important, and destined to be brought low. Comic baritone role requiring broad physical presence and delightful hypocrisy.
avoid: Menacing villain reading — Bumble is ridiculous, not dangerous

songs_to_prepare.title: Adelaide's Lament
songs_to_prepare.why: The pragmatic woman calculating her romantic options with comic desperation — Corney exactly

songs_to_prepare.title: Before the Parade Passes By
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano character deciding she is not going to miss her chance at status and comfort

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know
songs_to_prepare.why: Knowing comic soprano who is entirely aware of her own motivations and doesn't mind

oliver/widow-corney.style_guidance: Widow Corney is the workhouse matron engineering her own social advancement — soprano character role with comic calculation, warmth, and the specific menace of a woman who controls resources.
avoid: Purely benevolent matron reading — Corney is calculating her options in every scene

songs_to_prepare.title: Big Spender
songs_to_prepare.why: The working-class girl in a dangerous world — alto/mezzo with warmth and knowing street wisdom

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Tell Mama
songs_to_prepare.why: The cheerful companion who keeps her business to herself — alto with energy and comedy

oliver/bet.style_guidance: Bet is Nancy's friend and the show's secondary female role — alto/mezzo with warmth, street energy, and loyal sidekick quality. A supporting role who roots the Nancy story in community.
avoid: Lead weight material — Bet is supportive ensemble, not featured lead

oliver/ensemble-oliver.role_name: Ensemble — Workhouse Boys, Fagin's Gang, Street Sellers, Townspeople

songs_to_prepare.title: Consider Yourself
songs_to_prepare.why: The show's great welcoming ensemble number — street kids with personality and physical energy

songs_to_prepare.title: Who Will Buy
songs_to_prepare.why: The street sellers' morning ensemble — shows the breadth of character types needed

songs_to_prepare.title: Food, Glorious Food
songs_to_prepare.why: The opening ensemble — shows the workhouse boy treble quality for younger ensemble members

oliver/ensemble-oliver.style_guidance: Oliver! ensemble plays everything from starving orphans to cockney street sellers — period style, physical variety, and the ability to sell both joy and desperation convincingly.
avoid: Contemporary pop style — Oliver! is firmly in the British music hall / Golden Age tradition

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm Not That Girl
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who does not believe she belongs in the beautiful world she has glimpsed — mezzo belt with hope and doubt

songs_to_prepare.title: And I Am Telling You I'm Not Going
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo-soprano belt powerhouse — if the show needs a moment of pure vocal declaration for the role

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Rain on My Parade
songs_to_prepare.why: The girl who refuses to be defined by others' limits — mezzo belt with joy and self-determination

songs_to_prepare.title: Still Hurting
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — shows the raw emotional vulnerability beneath Vivian's performance of confidence

pretty-woman/vivian.style_guidance: Vivian is contemporary pop-mezzo with heart and humour — she is street-smart, funny, and genuinely kind. The vulnerability must coexist with the confidence. This is a mezzo with belt to F5 and a gift for making people root for her.
avoid: Passive, soft-voiced ingenue — Vivian has survived by being capable, present, and smart

songs_to_prepare.title: Being Alive
songs_to_prepare.why: The man who has everything and nothing — baritone confronting what is missing in a perfectly ordered life

songs_to_prepare.title: This Nearly Was Mine
songs_to_prepare.why: Romantic baritone who almost let happiness slip away — the moment Edward chooses to change

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: A controlled man claiming something he loves against all rational advice — Edward choosing Vivian

pretty-woman/edward.style_guidance: Edward is the closed-off, successful man who is opened by Vivian — baritone with intelligence, restrained warmth, and the capacity for a genuine transformation. He is not cold; he is defended.
avoid: Alpha villain-adjacent energy — Edward must be fundamentally a good man who lost his way, not a predator

songs_to_prepare.title: Broadway Baby
songs_to_prepare.why: The survivor with great dreams and a sharp tongue — alto/mezzo with wit and genuine loyalty

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Tell Mama
songs_to_prepare.why: The street-smart comedy mezzo who lives life on her own terms — Kit condensed

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm Still Here
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who has been through it all and is absolutely still standing — belt with resilience and heart

pretty-woman/kit-de-luca.style_guidance: Kit is the show's breakout comedy role — alto/mezzo belt with perfect comic timing, loyal heart, and the specific warmth of a best friend who speaks entirely in one-liners. She is funnier than the leads.
avoid: Tragic or self-pitying material — Kit's entire brand is defiant cheerfulness in the face of everything

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The theatrical host who sets up the story — character baritone with warmth and narrator energy

songs_to_prepare.title: Willkommen
songs_to_prepare.why: The MC who welcomes the audience into the story's world — knowing, warm, a little bit magic

pretty-woman/happy-man.style_guidance: The Happy Man is the story's theatrical guide — character baritone/tenor with warmth and the specific quality of someone who believes in the story they are telling. Both narrator and participant.
avoid: Detached narrator energy — the Happy Man loves this story and invests in its outcome

songs_to_prepare.title: Stars
songs_to_prepare.why: The character who believes the rules give him rights — tenor/baritone with cold entitlement

songs_to_prepare.title: Epiphany
songs_to_prepare.why: A man whose mask of civility slips to reveal ugliness — the real Stuckey under pressure

pretty-woman/philip-stuckey.style_guidance: Stuckey is the villain who believes he is the victim — tenor/baritone with polished surface and genuine menace. He genuinely cannot comprehend that Vivian is more than a transaction.
avoid: Over-theatrical villainy — Stuckey's danger is in his plausibility and sense of entitlement

songs_to_prepare.title: Make Them Hear You
songs_to_prepare.why: The older industrialist who is being broken up — baritone with dignity and the sadness of seeing your life's work dismantled

pretty-woman/james-morse.style_guidance: James Morse is the target of Edward's corporate raid who becomes Edward's conscience — bass-baritone with warmth, age, and the moral weight of someone who built something real.
avoid: Defeated or weak reading — Morse is dignified even in his situation; he is the show's moral anchor

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The son who has watched his father's world be threatened — baritone/tenor with complicated loyalty

pretty-woman/david-morse.style_guidance: David Morse is a secondary supporting character — baritone/tenor relationship to James Morse. Shows the human cost of Edward's corporate world. Secondary ensemble role.
avoid: Scene-stealing choices — David is a supporting character who serves the larger moral story

songs_to_prepare.title: Sempre libera
songs_to_prepare.why: This IS Violetta's number — soprano with genuine operatic technique showing the scene's parallel to Vivian

songs_to_prepare.title: Glitter and Be Gay
songs_to_prepare.why: The operatic soprano with layers — the woman performing for the world while feeling everything

pretty-woman/violetta.style_guidance: Violetta appears in the La Traviata opera sequence — a genuine operatic soprano with classical technique is required. This is not a musical theatre belt moment; it is a real opera scene.
avoid: Musical theatre belt approach — the opera sequence requires authentic classical soprano technique

songs_to_prepare.title: Make Someone Happy
songs_to_prepare.why: Warm hotel concierge tenor who genuinely wishes the characters well — service and sincerity

pretty-woman/giulio.style_guidance: Giulio is the Regent Beverly Wilshire concierge who sees everything — warm tenor with discretion, warmth, and the hotel-staff ability to understand without judging. Supporting character.
avoid: Flashy or foregrounded choices — Giulio enables the story, he does not compete with it

songs_to_prepare.title: Brindisi (Libiamo)
songs_to_prepare.why: Alfredo's operatic tenor number — requires authentic classical tenor technique in the opera scene

pretty-woman/alfredo.style_guidance: Alfredo appears in the La Traviata opera sequence — genuine operatic tenor technique required. The scene's power depends on authentic classical performance.
avoid: Musical theatre belt approach — authentic opera is the requirement for this scene

pretty-woman/ensemble-pretty.role_name: Ensemble — Beverly Hills Society, Hollywood Boulevard, Store Clerks, Opera Guests

songs_to_prepare.title: Shout
songs_to_prepare.why: The show's contemporary pop-rock ensemble — shows the rock-musical voice required

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Rain on My Parade
songs_to_prepare.why: Female ensemble belt energy — the Hollywood Boulevard women with attitude and drive

pretty-woman/ensemble-pretty.style_guidance: Pretty Woman ensemble operates in two worlds: contemporary pop-rock Los Angeles and the classical opera house. Versatile voices that can handle both, with strong character work for both worlds.
avoid: Single-register approach — the ensemble must convincingly span street and society
